newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to celebrate export of oil on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to celebrate export of oil on Tuesday.

text.p: Iraq is planning a celebration to mark the resumption of its oil exports to world markets on Tuesday, official newspapers said on Monday.
Iraqi oil will flow for the first time since United Nations sanctions were imposed on Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The newspapers said the oil ministry would hold a big celebration in the northern oil centre of Kirkuk where senior officials would turn on the tap early on Tuesday, unleashing the partial exports under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the U.N.
"World television networks, foreign reporters and representatives of local and Arab media have been invited," the newspapers said.
"Tomorrow our oil flows," said the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya in a front-page banner headline.
Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Friday he expected Iraqi oil exports to resume early on Tuesday. The newspapers said the zero hour would be at 8 a.m. (0500 GMT).
Iraq last month agreed to U.N. conditions on limited exports of $2 billion in six months on a renewable basis to help it buy food and medicine to alleviate suffering of its sanctions-hit population.
